results.reason: Issue B quotes §14.2: a change of more than 50% ownership is deemed an assignment needing Vantrell's prior written consent, with a 30-day termination right. It says the 100% stock sale triggers this, Schedule 4.4 says 'None', and the §7.2(c) condition covers only consents listed on Schedule 4.4.

Issue G explains under §16.1 that the Company needs Supplier consent to assign while Supplier may assign freely. It flags the risk of assignment to a competitor or less reliable supplier, leaving the sole-source supply in their hands.

Issue A calculates the 120-day notice deadline as September 2, 2026, notes the SPA was dated September 21, 2026, and concludes the agreement will expire absent prior exercise. It ties the fix to the Extension Pricing.

Issue C explains that Side Letter §2 limits Fundamental Reps to 4.1 and 4.2 and that §11.11 gives the Side Letter priority. Its table shows 4.3 and 4.12 become subject to the $8.45M cap and the deductible.
Issue D identifies Delaware law and Chancery in Side Letter §6.1/6.2 versus New York in SPA §11.8/11.9. It explains that the Side Letter's priority splits indemnity disputes from other disputes.
States the cap is $8,450,000, or 10% of the Purchase Price.
States that §11.11 gives the Side Letter first priority, ahead of the SPA.
The memo is addressed to [Partner]. Each issue is a distinct lettered item with documents and sections, a 'Why this matters' explanation, and a recommended action.
Opens with 'Issues Requiring Immediate Client Call', lists additional issues in order of significance, and includes a summary table of client call items.
Never says the option remains exercisable; it states the deadline passed and the window could only be met if notice was already given.
Correctly states the Side Letter controls and that 4.3 and 4.12 are capped as currently drafted.
